Migration guide (v1 → v2) v1 retired

v1 reached end of life on 2026-08-01 alongside the webhooks GA changelog entry. This guide covers the three breaking changes you need to handle to move a v1 integration to v2.

1. Pagination: offset → cursor

v1 used page/per_page query parameters. v2 uses an opaque cursor and next_cursor — see Limits, quotas & errors for the exact envelope.

diff diff 
- GET /v1/pipelines?page=2&per_page=20
+ GET /v2/pipelines?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjIwfQ

2. Status checks: polling → webhooks

v1 had no push notifications — you polled a pipeline's status endpoint. v2 replaces this with the Webhooks endpoint: subscribe to pipeline.completed and pipeline.failed instead of polling.

3. Error shape

v1 returned bare error strings. v2 wraps every error in an object with a stable code field. Update any error handling that matched on message text — see the error shape reference.

v1 is retired

v1 endpoints no longer accept requests. If you're seeing 404s on /v1/* paths, that's why — there is no grace-period fallback.

Still stuck?

Common migration issues are covered in Troubleshooting / FAQ.

Start with Pipelines

Godzilla is built from three ideas that compose into everything else in these docs. Understanding how they relate makes the rest of the platform — guides, API reference, SDKs — much easier to follow.

Concept

Pipelines

Named, versioned workflows that move data from a source to a destination through optional transforms.

Connectors

Pre-built integrations to external systems — sources, destinations, or both.

Events

The atomic unit of data flowing through a pipeline, plus the platform's own lifecycle events.

How event payload shapes are declared and validated using JSON Schema.

How they fit together

A pipeline reads events from a source connector, transforms them, and writes them to a destination connector. You can assign schemas to validate that events match your expected data structure before processing. Everything else in Godzilla — retries, webhooks, monitoring — is built on top of that single loop.

Pipelines

A pipeline is the core unit of work in Godzilla: a named, versioned data-processing workflow that moves data from a source connector, through zero or more transform steps, to a destination connector. Every pipeline runs as a sequence of events flowing through that path.

Anatomy of a pipeline

Every pipeline has three parts:

  • Source — the connector that emits events into the pipeline (a database, a queue, an upload, a webhook).
  • Transforms — an ordered list of steps that reshape, filter, or enrich events as they pass through. Transforms are optional; a pipeline with none is a pass-through copy.
  • Destination — the connector that events are written to once transforms complete.
Pipelines are declarative

You describe the desired source, transforms, and destination; Godzilla schedules and retries the runs. You never manage worker processes directly.

Pipeline state

A pipeline is always in one of three states:

  • draft — configured but not yet processing events.
  • active — running on its configured schedule or trigger.
  • paused — temporarily stopped; resumes from the last checkpoint.

Versioning

Pipeline configuration is versioned. Publishing a new version does not affect events already in flight on the previous version — in-flight runs finish on the version they started on. This matters most when a pipeline definition is part of a larger migration; see the Migration guide for an example of retiring an old pipeline version safely.

Schemas

A schema defines the expected shape and structure of an event's payload. Schemas allow you to declare what fields an event should contain, what types they should be, and which fields are required. Godzilla validates incoming events against their schema and can route invalid events to your pipeline's dead-letter queue.

Schema definition

Schemas are declared as JSON Schema documents. Each schema specifies the properties expected in an event's payload field, plus validation constraints.

order-event-schema.json json 
{
  "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
  "title": "Order Event",
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "order_id": { "type": "string" },
    "customer_id": { "type": "string" },
    "amount_cents": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 },
    "currency": { "type": "string", "default": "USD" },
    "items": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": { "type": "object" }
    }
  },
  "required": ["order_id", "customer_id", "amount_cents"]
}

Validation and error handling

When a pipeline receives an event, Godzilla validates it against the assigned schema before processing. If validation fails:

  • The event is marked as failed.
  • A validation error detail is recorded.
  • The event is routed through the standard retry loop with exponential backoff.
  • After the retry limit is exhausted, the event is moved to the pipeline's dead-letter queue.
Schema validation timing

Validation occurs as soon as an event is ingested, before any transforms are applied. This ensures that all downstream processing operates on data that matches expectations.

Assigning schemas to event types

Schemas are assigned to event types at the pipeline level. An event type like order.created can be validated against a specific schema version, and you can update the schema independently when your data model evolves.

pipeline-config.json json 
{
  "pipeline": "order-ingestion",
  "source": "connector_kafka_orders",
  "schemas": {
    "order.created": {
      "version": "1.0",
      "definition": ... 
    },
    "order.updated": {
      "version": "1.0",
      "definition": ...
    }
  }
}

Versioning and evolution

Schemas support semantic versioning, allowing you to evolve your event structure safely:

  • Patch updates (1.0.1) — Fix validation rules without changing the structure.
  • Minor updates (1.1.0) — Add optional fields or loosen constraints.
  • Major updates (2.0.0) — Change required fields or restructure the payload.

When you update a schema, existing pipelines continue using their pinned version until you explicitly roll forward, giving you time to test and migrate downstream systems.

Schema defaults

If no schema is assigned to an event type, Godzilla does not validate the payload — all events pass through without structural checks. You can add schemas incrementally as your pipelines mature.

Dead-letter queue inspection

Invalid events appear in your pipeline's dead-letter queue with detailed error metadata, letting you audit failures and reprocess events once the underlying issue is fixed. See Handling errors & retries for how to drain and replay dead-lettered events.

Quotas & billing

Godzilla operates on a tiered plan system. Each plan includes a monthly request quota and a per-minute rate limit. When you exceed your plan's limits, the API begins returning 429 Too Many Requests responses.

Plan tiers

The following table shows the request quota and rate limit for each plan tier:

Plan Monthly Quota Rate Limit Features
Free 10,000 requests 100 req/min Community support, single workspace
Standard 1,000,000 requests 1,000 req/min Email support, team access, webhooks
Professional 10,000,000 requests 5,000 req/min Priority support, audit logs, SSO
Enterprise Custom Custom Dedicated support, SLA, on-premise options

All rate limits are per workspace, not per API key. If your team shares a workspace, the rate limit applies to the aggregate request volume across all keys.

Rate limits

Each API response includes rate-limit headers that tell you your current quota status:

  • X-RateLimit-Limit — Your per-minute request allowance.
  • X-RateLimit-Remaining — Requests remaining in this minute.
  • X-RateLimit-Reset — Unix timestamp when the window resets.

When a request would exceed your per-minute limit, the server responds with 429 Too Many Requests and a Retry-After header indicating how many seconds to wait before retrying. Respect this header — retrying before the window resets will continue to fail.

rate-limit-headers.txt text 
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 847
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1704067200

Monthly quota

Beyond the per-minute rate limit, each plan includes a monthly request quota. The quota resets on the first day of each month (UTC). Your plan tier determines your monthly allowance.

You can monitor your monthly usage in the workspace settings dashboard. There's no 429 response for exceeding monthly quota — instead, your workspace becomes quota_exceeded and all API requests fail with 403 Forbidden. Read the error body for instructions on how to upgrade or purchase additional quota.

Quota exceeded blocks the entire workspace

Once monthly quota is exceeded, all API operations halt until your quota resets or your plan tier increases. This includes reads, writes, and webhook deliveries. Plan accordingly and monitor usage during high-traffic periods.

What happens when you exceed your quota

Per-minute rate limit (429)

If you send more than your plan's per-minute limit in a single calendar minute, the excess requests receive a 429 Too Many Requests response. The API is still functional — you can retry after the window resets or after the time specified in Retry-After.

How to recover: Implement exponential backoff with jitter. Read the Retry-After header and wait at least that many seconds before retrying. If you regularly hit the rate limit, consider upgrading your plan tier or caching API responses.

Monthly quota exceeded (403)

Once your workspace's aggregate monthly request count reaches your plan's quota, all subsequent requests return 403 Forbidden with the error code quota_exceeded:

quota-exceeded-error.json json 
{
  "error": {
    "code": "quota_exceeded",
    "message": "Monthly request quota exhausted. Upgrade your plan or purchase additional quota.",
    "request_id": "req_abc123"
  }
}

How to recover: Upgrade to a higher plan tier or purchase additional monthly quota. Only workspace admins can manage billing and upgrades — visit the Godzilla web console and navigate to Settings > Billing. The quota resets automatically on the first day of the next month.

Upgrading and custom quotas

To upgrade your plan or request a custom quota, log in to the Godzilla web console:

  1. Navigate to Settings > Billing.
  2. Review your current plan and monthly usage.
  3. Select a higher tier or contact sales for a custom arrangement.

Enterprise plans and on-premise deployments are handled by our sales team — email sales@godzilladocs.dev with details about your use case and expected monthly volume.

Usage monitoring

Set up workspace alerts to notify you when your monthly usage approaches 80% of your quota. This gives you time to upgrade or adjust your integration before hitting the hard limit.
